svg.text: Data Plane — Two-Tier Route & Tenant Isolation
Per-request path from tenant browser to Bedrock · three-tier route cache · one microVM per tenant with four base disks plus an optional credential disk
TLS termination · caching disabled · no WAF
resolves the tenant route, proxies onward
How the edge finds a tenant
The edge resolves route:{tenant} from the fastest
tier that still has it, falling back downward on a miss.
On a cache/Valkey miss the edge serves a static
error — it never guesses another tenant's microVM.
route:{tenant} is written only after the microVM
passes its promotion gate — the tenant becomes
routable exactly when it is actually ready.
No TTL on the route entry: a healthy tenant never
silently expires out of the routing table.
The route value carries the host's DNAT port, so
the edge always targets the correct guest gateway
The edge terminates the tenant hop; the microVM
accepts no inbound connection from the internet.
Route cache and Valkey are read-only on the request
path — no tenant input can rewrite another's route.
Tenant microVM — four base disks + optional credential disk
one Firecracker microVM per tenant, dedicated kernel
boot args pin the root device; drives attached in fixed order
data · per-VM writable volume (config lives here)
Identity + safety skills are read-only — a change needs a new image.
Each tenant runs in its own Firecracker microVM with a
dedicated guest kernel — no shared runtime or process space.
East-west traffic between microVMs is dropped at the host
The guest holds no AWS credentials. Identity and safety
skills are cold-injected onto read-only disks before boot.
IMDS is blocked and the credentials disk is hardware
write-protected. Egress allow-list and DNS Firewall are
config-gated, off by default — until then egress is open.
Measured: microVM boot 1.74s p50 · launch→gateway 6.48s · cross-tenant 100% packet loss · blank-VM RSS ~609 MB
